title: Tteokbokki
subtitle: Spicy stir-fried rice cakes in gochujang sauce
excerpt: Tteokbokki is a beloved Korean street food of chewy cylindrical rice cakes cooked in a bold, sweet-spicy gochujang sauce. Fish cakes and spring onions are added to the broth and everything is cooked together until the sauce thickens and coats the rice cakes.
sourceNotes: Tteokbokki as a spicy street food dates to the 1950s, when a vendor in Seoul's Sindang-dong market began cooking rice cakes in a gochujang sauce. Earlier versions of the dish used soy sauce and were considered a royal palace food. The modern spicy version became one of Korea's most iconic street foods.

glossaryTerms.definition: Korean rice cakes made from pounded or ground glutinous or short-grain rice. They come in many shapes. The cylindrical variety used in tteokbokki, called garae-tteok, is long and smooth with a dense, chewy texture.

Korean fish cake made from ground white fish, flour, and seasoning, then formed into flat sheets and fried. It has a springy, mild texture and absorbs spicy sauces well. It is sold in blocks in the refrigerated section of Korean supermarkets.

content.text: Tteokbokki takes 25 minutes and serves 4. These chewy
rice cakes are cooked in a sticky, spicy sauce until they absorb the flavour and turn glossy. Add
fish cakes to make it more substantial.

If the rice cakes are frozen, soak them in warm water for 10 to 15 minutes first until they soften. Fresh rice cakes can go straight into the pan. The sauce should be quite loose when you start cooking. It thickens as the rice cakes release their starch. Do not add extra thickener.
Make a quick stock: simmer the dried anchovies in 600ml of water for 10 minutes. Strain and discard the anchovies. You will have about 500ml of stock.
Add the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar, and garlic to the stock. Stir to combine. Bring to a boil in a wide frying pan.
Add the rice cakes and spring onions. Cook over a medium-high heat, stirring regularly, for 12 to 15 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the rice cakes.
The rice cakes are ready when they are soft and chewy and the sauce has reduced to a thick coating. Stir in the sesame oil off the heat.
Scatter sesame seeds over the top. Serve immediately from the pan.

items.symptom: Rice cakes are still hard after 15 minutes
items.cause: They were frozen and not soaked beforehand
items.fix: Soak frozen rice cakes in warm water for 15 to 20 minutes before cooking. They should feel pliable before going into the sauce.

items.symptom: Sauce is too thick and the rice cakes are sticking to the pan
items.cause: Too much liquid evaporated during cooking
items.fix: Add a splash of water or extra stock to loosen the sauce. Stir frequently to prevent the rice cakes from catching on the bottom.

items.cause: Sugar was not balanced against the gochujang
items.fix: Reduce the sugar to 1 tbsp next time. Add a few drops of fish sauce or soy sauce to bring back the savoury balance.

content.text: Tteokbokki is a Korean street food. It is sold at pojangmacha stalls across Korea. It is cheap and filling. Students eat it after school. It is also made at home on weeknights. It is one of the most recognisable Korean dishes.
